sections.title: Form and leaves
sections.text: Plantago major, greater plantain, is a perennial rosette herb with broad oval to heart-shaped leaves and several prominent parallel veins. The broad blades contrast with the narrow leaves of ribwort plantain, P. lanceolata.

sections.title: Flowers and fruits
sections.text: Small flowers are crowded on long, slender spikes. The dry capsules contain seeds; the number varies among plants.

sections.title: Food
sections.text: The youngest leaves can be eaten raw in salads. Older leaves are tougher and are better cooked with the main veins removed.
